newsitem.title: USA: Most fund buyers use advisors - survey.
newsitem.headline: Most fund buyers use advisors - survey.

text.p: The majority of mutual fund investors use financial advisors rather than buying funds directly, according to a survey conducted for a mutual fund trade group.
The study found that 60 percent exclusively used advisors, while 27 percent bought directly and 13 percent used both. The study was conducted by Yankelovich Partners for Mutual Fund Forum.

"Despite the development of numerous new sources of personal finance information and new methods of purchase, consumers continue to depend on professional financial advisors to buy mutual funds," the group said.
The typical profile of an investor is middle-aged, college educated, with an average salary of $61,700 and $90,000 in assets, the survey found.
About 56 percent are ages 35 and 59 and 51 percent are college educated, the survey found.
The survey nationally sampled 564 investors of long-term funds nationally June 12-23.
